overall: The AG found the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by deliberating by email on seven dates, ordered release of those emails, but found no violation in the executive session and other email allegations and declined to find intent.

allegations.summary: A quorum of the Board allegedly deliberated by email about Estabrook Road, outside a posted meeting, roughly 31 times between 2016 and 2018.
allegations.key_passage: We find that emails exchanged on March 29-30, 2016; April 6, 2016; August 2, 2016; June 9, 2017; September 12, 2017; November 16, 2017; and January 12, 2018, contain improper deliberations because these emails reached a quorum of the Board

allegations.summary: Emails from the Town Manager sent to a quorum of the Board were alleged to be improper deliberation.
allegations.key_passage: the Town Manager is not a member of the Board or otherwise subject to the Open Meeting Law, and thus, any emails sent by him to a quorum of the Board do not constitute improper deliberation.

allegations.summary: Emails of October 26, 2017, May 9, 2018, and May 14, 2018 were alleged to be deliberation among a quorum.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the emails exchanged on October 26, 2017; May 9, 2018; and May 14, 2018, contained either scheduling or procedural information, or were administrative in nature, and are therefore exempt from the definition of deliberation under the law.

allegations.summary: Whether the email deliberation violations were intentional, which would weigh on the penalty analysis under the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we also do not find that the Board acted with deliberate ignorance of the law, and we decline to find that this violation was intentional.

allegations.summary: Executive sessions of September 20, 2016, December 12, 2016, and March 27, 2017 were alleged to have improperly discussed Estabrook Road.
The October 16, 2017 executive session on Estabrook Road litigation was alleged to be an improper use of the litigation purpose.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the discussions during the October 16, 2017, executive session meeting pertained to a decision to pursue litigation against the Estabrook Road landowners and therefore the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law by meeting under Purpose 3.

allegations.summary: The November 29, 2016 and June 19, 2017 executive sessions on Estabrook Road litigation strategy were alleged to be improper, and the noticed litigation topics were not identified.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Board properly met in executive session and that it was also reasonable to conclude that announcing the specific topic of litigation prior to convening in executive session would have comprised the purpose for the executive sessions and alerted the potential litigants.

remedy: Publicly release the seven emails found to be improper deliberations within 30 days of receipt of the determination, if not already done.
Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements.
remedy_passage: We order the Board to publicly release these emails within 30 days of receipt of this determination, if it has not already done so.
